findings: Verified exact patch application and byte accounting between before docs/NATIVE-CORE.md (35,785 bytes, 557 lines, SHA-256 14efb29a17b61ad69e24bbb5163a7ab62df464cbfc976a20b24b9ea52ee9f00b) and after docs/NATIVE-CORE.md (36,959 bytes, 569 lines, SHA-256 904bddfaa9eabe49f5e935a6e704ca65500a2edb975e17500bd56088b783adce) across all hunks (+1,174 bytes total).

Confirmed against baseline/Cargo.toml, baseline/crates/mori/Cargo.toml, and baseline/packages/moriarty-beta/package.json that the Node @moriarty-lang/beta package exposes a bin entry named mori (dist/cli.js) for the beta profile, while cargo run -p mori --locked -- from the repository root unambiguously selects the Rust workspace package mori with its default native feature enabled.

Confirmed against baseline/crates/mori/Cargo.toml and baseline/crates/mori/src/cli.rs that the introductory paragraph accurately reflects the default native feature versus a --no-default-features build (local Core reference tooling only, whereas Midnight compile/call/proof, targeted inspection with --target, simulate --trace, replay, and JubJub signed owner-intent profiles require native).

Confirmed against baseline/crates/mori/src/commands/init.rs that generated starter README.md files instruct running mori check source.mori --json, mori simulate source.mori --action {action} --scenario scenario.json, and mori test . from the generated project directory; the updated guide accurately preserves the project cwd requirement and instructs replacing the README's unqualified mori executable with an absolute path to the Rust binary built from this checkout.

Confirmed that all actual command invocations in docs/NATIVE-CORE.md (both shell blocks and inline command synopses) now use cargo run -p mori --locked -- while preserving every existing subcommand, flag, operand, relative path, line continuation, and shell redirection, and leaving cargo test --workspace --locked unchanged.

Confirmed against baseline/docs/MORIARTY-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md that the documentation update makes no standalone installation, runtime/proof execution, or external submission qualification claims, and does not alter public permissions, security/native limits, or default/Core/beta behavior.
